policy.authority: Benchmark targets are the future source of truth. Evidence Kit is a legacy import/report archive during migration.
policy.benchmarkCode: Benchmark implementation lives with the runtime/package code it measures.
policy.activeLoops: Autoresearch sessions optimize one target id at a time and own only active loop state.
policy.docs: Docs and research files are linked evidence, not benchmark control state.

targets.question: Does a schema-backed sparse edit keep the changed representation span and untouched boundary identities local inside one deep, wide top-level node?

metrics.upgrade: A sparse schema-backed edit must retain untouched boundary identities and change fewer than 64 tokens. The 100/1,000/10,000/50,000 timing rows are labeled immutable-publication diagnostic because they measure immutable DocumentChange ancestor publication, not schema construction.

correctness.policy: Promotion requires contextual fitter laws, strict direct-write rejection, mapped selection/runtime identity, canonical idempotence, a sentinel proving the benchmark's compiled schema is active, and the strict locality benchmark.

targets.question: What does immutable clone, validation, and preparation cost at 10, 100, 1,000, and 10,000 nodes, and does trusted ContentSlice reuse identity and preparation without size-dependent work?

metrics.upgrade: Record closed and untrusted fromJSON clone-plus-validation-and-preparation p50/p95/p99 alongside trusted identity and preparation reuse at 10, 100, 1,000, and 10,000 nodes. Promotion requires exact source isolation, deep freezing, trusted identity reuse, and trusted preparation reuse; latency remains baseline-only until comparable runs justify a target.

correctness.policy: The live ContentSlice API must own immutable snapshots, trusted identity reuse, and trusted preparation reuse, while this registered benchmark remains the single metric and artifact authority.

thresholds.promotion: plite_content_slice_value_trusted_identity_reuse=1 and plite_content_slice_value_trusted_preparation_reuse=1 and plite_content_slice_value_source_alias_free=1 and plite_content_slice_value_deeply_frozen=1; timing metrics are baseline-only

targets.question: Does schema architecture stay bounded across 1/100/1,000 contributions, 100/1,000 Plate descriptors, local construction and schema deltas, equivalent/non-equivalent configuration, 10k-block migration, projected clipboard, type inference, and the established compiled corpus?

metrics.upgrade: Preserve every established compile/query/validation/invalidation/cache/heap gate. Add exact 1/100/1,000 contribution compile/cache counts; 100/1,000 Plate descriptor resolution plus cold and structurally cached startup; isolated createAndFill construction-plan cardinality across 100/1,000 irrelevant defaults; equivalent and non-equivalent Plate publication; 1k/10k explicit migration; fixed two-node canonical open-edge projected clipboard locality across 1k/50k documents; and 100/1,000 TypeScript fixture budgets with an explicit 1,000-plugin widening boundary.

correctness.command: bun test --preload ./config/plite-source-test-setup.ts ./packages/plite/test/schema-target-model-oracle.test.ts ./packages/plite/test/schema-compiler-laws.test.ts ./packages/plite/test/schema-compiler.test.ts ./packages/plite/test/incremental-schema-validation.test.ts ./packages/plite-react/test/schema-runtime-invalidation-contract.test.ts ./packages/core/src/internal/plugin/compilePlateModel.spec.ts ./benchmarks/editor/benchmarks/plite-schema-architecture-benchmark.test.ts && pnpm --filter @platejs/plite-react exec vitest run --config ./vitest.config.mjs test/projected-clipboard-contract.test.ts
correctness.policy: Promotion keeps the existing compiler/property/incremental/schema-delta contracts and additionally requires Plate model publication, canonical projected clipboard behavior, exact workload cohorts, explicit type widening, and every strict execution budget.

targets.question: Does detached fitContent work scale with the immutable slice and parent rather than unrelated editor-root or schema width?

metrics.upgrade: Warm fitting of one fixed detached parent/slice must remain within 1.5x across 10 to 50,000 unrelated editor blocks and 5 to 100 declared element types. Cold editor setup and 1/10/100-node slice timings remain absolute baselines.

correctness.policy: Every measured fit must validate under the detached parent, remain deterministic and idempotent, and publish no editor state or commit.

thresholds.promotion: plite_fit_content_document_width_ratio<=1.5 and plite_fit_content_schema_width_ratio<=1.5 and zero fit correctness failures or editor commits; slice-size and cold-editor rows are baseline-only

targets.question: Does a sparse edit schedule only matching correction events for touched nodes and ancestors as document width grows?

metrics.upgrade: A property write must schedule exactly the matching properties and content corrections, never children corrections or unrelated siblings, through the 50,000-block cohort.

correctness.policy: Promotion requires composed-change classification, runtime-ID remapping, fixed-point/cycle laws, force repair, root lifecycle, and strict sparse touched-count proof.

targets.question: Does command dispatch scale across 0, 1, 8, and 32 handlers, keep simple fallback continuation-free and document-size independent, and bound prefix composition without pretending its generic TransactionSpec cost is command-only work?

metrics.upgrade: Every simple and prefix lane must stay within its explicit absolute p50/p95 budget. Simple dispatch at 20,000 blocks must remain within 2x its 100-block p50 at every handler depth. Runtime proof observes zero callable continuation identities in simple handlers and one fresh identity per around visit. Prefix document-size ratios are recorded only because each handler intentionally constructs a generic immutable TransactionSpec. The synthetic same-run interpreter is a correctness and machine-noise control, never a replacement for the unavailable pre-edit baseline.

correctness.policy: Promotion requires command fallback/prefix/rollback/configuration laws, exact actual/reference visit and handled-result parity, exact callable-continuation identity evidence, zero no-op commits, fixed absolute latency budgets, and the simple large-document ratio gate.

thresholds.promotion: plite_command_dispatch_worst_budget_ratio<=1 and simple 20k/100-block p50 ratio<=2 and plite_command_dispatch_continuation_failures=0 and plite_command_dispatch_reference_parity=1; prefix document-size ratio is record-only

targets.question: Does the cost of one history-skipped remote commit stay independent of retained undo depth?

metrics.upgrade: At equal 1,000-commit remote bursts, depth 1,000 must stay within 4x the depth-100 median and p95 while lazy undo resolves exactly.

correctness.policy: The benchmark gate requires immutable depth clipping, lazy/eager equivalence, explicit mapping failure, and exact undo after the burst.

targets.question: Does one sparse Yjs edit stay local and distance-independent across a 10,000-block root?

metrics.upgrade: Start, middle, and end edits must keep local and sync medians within 2x, decode one top-level node, retain one changed range, and keep runtime-ID p95 below 1ms.

correctness.policy: The performance claim requires exact event-native traces, narrow changed ranges, full event-shape coverage, and explicit fallback tests.

targets.question: Does Slate v2 beat legacy Slate for 5,000-block React editing, selection, startup, and full-document replacement?
targets.command: REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_LEGACY_REPO=../slate REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_DISPOSE_DELAY_MS=0 REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_SPLIT_SELECTION=1 REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_ISOLATE_SURFACES=1 REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_SURFACES=v2DefaultRenderAuto,v2DomPresent REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_BLOCKS=5000 REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_ITERATIONS=5 REACT_HUGE_COMPARE_TYPE_OPS=10 bun benchmarks/slate-v2/donor/browser/react/huge-document-legacy-compare.mjs

metrics.upgrade: Primary metric is the worst p95 ratio across the 5,000-block default/render-auto and DOM-present product lanes versus legacy chunking-on.

correctness.policy: Promotion requires the benchmark p95 ratio plus the fast Slate v2 check suite.

thresholds.stop: stop when the promotion target is stable across two correctness-green repeat packets or when the remaining owner needs architecture work

targets.question: Does Slate v2 stay fast and local across the full huge-document benchmark suite?
targets.command: HUGE_DOC_FULL_STRICT_BUDGET=1 HUGE_DOC_FULL_LEGACY_REPO=../slate HUGE_DOC_FULL_BLOCKS=5000 HUGE_DOC_FULL_ITERATIONS=5 HUGE_DOC_FULL_TRACE_ITERATIONS=5 HUGE_DOC_FULL_TYPE_OPS=10 bun benchmarks/slate-v2/donor/browser/react/huge-document-full.mjs

metrics.upgrade: Primary metric is the worst normalized budget ratio across core huge-doc ops, React legacy compare, browser type-to-paint, click latency, cold and materialized selection, model-backed typing, DOM budget, long-task, listener, selector, and overlay locality lanes. Strict budget mode must be enabled so over-budget rows fail instead of only printing metrics.

correctness.policy: Promotion requires the aggregate suite metric at or below budget, zero react_huge_doc_full_budget_failure_count, zero react_huge_doc_full_failure_count, and the fast Slate v2 check suite.

thresholds.plateau: stop after 2 correctness-green packets with less than 5% gain
